provinceTextScope: Bataan; 47 NMNH Material Samples and 19 iBOL material-sample keys linked by the preceding broad GBIF coordinate screen
question: Do the 66 NMNH/iBOL GBIF material-sample keys represent 66 independently captured Bataan fish, and do they resolve capture locality, taxon identity, or reusable species images?

metadataCrosswalkSnapshot.retained: Aggregate counts and a bounded voucher/accession/date/name crosswalk; no nucleotide sequence text, exact coordinates, or media retained.

recordRepresentation.interpretation: The 66 GBIF occurrence keys are dataset representations of 47 cataloged USNM vouchers plus 19 linked iBOL material-sample records; they are not 66 independent fish or capture events.

sourceDisagreements: Two vouchers labeled Pennahia anea in NMNH material metadata are named Pennahia aneus in GenBank organism metadata; retain this as a nomenclature/source-label discrepancy rather than silently standardizing it.
One NMNH material row is genus-level Pempheris while its linked GenBank record names Pempheris schwenkii; the sequence submitter label alone is not an independent museum redetermination.

sequenceVoucherCrosswalk.interpretation: Public GenBank feature metadata cross-links each iBOL sample to the same USNM voucher and collection date. These fields confirm record linkage, not the specimen's field capture station or a new taxonomic determination.

collectionAndLocalityContext.interpretation: Market location and vendor-supplied origin statements are not georeferenced capture stations. Broad, overlapping waterBody labels and coordinates with more than 1 km uncertainty do not resolve capture water or a Bataan-only occurrence.

fdaDetailRecord.metadataContext: Smithsonian Institution NMNH, market survey, Philippines

externalReferenceCrosscheck.interpretation: The FDA RSSL record provides a useful external voucher/taxon/accession cross-link for this sample and describes a market-survey context; it does not identify a capture water or validate the other 18 vouchers. The linked image was not viewed or reused.

mediaAndReuse.interpretation: Dataset metadata licenses do not establish image-specific reuse rights or approve biological claims. No image was reviewed, copied, or added.

interpretation.decision: Close this bounded item-level crosswalk task, but keep its market-origin specimen and linked sequence records in research-only status. The 19 voucher/accession/date links clarify catalog relationships; they do not establish Bataan capture sites or a wild-waterbody inventory. The 66 GBIF keys are not 66 distinct fish. Preserve source-name conflicts and do not use the FDA reference image.

limitations: The Bataan GBIF filter is an indexed administrative-text candidate screen, not a verified provincial boundary or capture locality.
Market and vendor statements are unverified origin claims and can refer to places outside Bataan.
Coordinates have more than 1,000 m uncertainty and are not used for waterbody geometry or occurrence assignment.
GenBank voucher and collection-date qualifiers establish cross-record linkage but are submitter-supplied metadata and do not independently identify a capture station or resolve taxonomy.

The FDA RSSL is designed for seafood identification and includes authenticated, often-vouchered reference specimens, but its market-survey provenance does not establish a Philippine wild capture locality.
No image was examined; record or dataset license metadata is not blanket permission to reuse specimen photographs.
This review is not a complete taxonomic checklist for Bataan, Manila Bay, or Central Luzon.
nextStep: Continue L3 source discovery with independent, taxon-resolved freshwater and brackish surveys in Central Luzon, then continue distinct wetland, estuary, and marine waterbody leads. Prioritize date, site-level methods, voucher or accession, and item-specific reuse evidence; preserve shared Manila Bay records and do not assign market-vendor claims to capture waters.
